items.title: Stochastic supplement: Shared-noise sphere energy balance

source.anchor: Complete source-only.json: D1-D6, A1-A5, F1-F3, P1-P6 and B1-B5
source.attribution: Original exposition of a classical supplied-solution stochastic identity; no novelty claim or attribution to a textbook theorem number.

items.statement: Let \(E=\mathbb R^d\), \(S=\{x\in E:\|x\|=1\}\), and \(C=S^N\), with \(N>0\). On one probability space with a complete right-continuous filtration, let each \(B_i\) be a standard \(E\)-valued Brownian motion relative to that filtration. Let \(X_i,Y_i\) be supplied jointly measurable, strongly progressive processes taking values in \(S\). Fix \(\lambda\ge0\) and continuous fields \(b_X,b_Y:[0,\infty)\times C\times C\to E^N\). Assume the coordinate integral forms of the displayed SDEs hold on every positive finite horizon, almost surely simultaneously at every time on that horizon. The two equations for particle \(i\) use the same \(B_i\). Then the expected normalized squared chord separation has the exact integral and derivative identities below. With the negative-time clamping convention, \(G\) is also continuous and locally integrable on all of \(\mathbb R\); these are conclusions of the theorem.
assumptions: \(N\) is a positive natural number and \(d\) is a natural number. The exact identity imposes no \(d\ge3\) condition. When \(d=0\), the existence of the supplied sphere-valued processes on a probability space is impossible, so that case is vacuous.

All processes use the same probability measure and filtration. Each \(B_i\) starts at zero, is strongly adapted, and has continuous paths almost surely. For \(s<t\), the increment \(B_i(t)-B_i(s)\) is centered Gaussian with covariance \((t-s)I\), independent of the entire past filtration at \(s\). Independence between the drivers of different particles is not required.

Each \(X_i,Y_i\) is jointly measurable in time and sample and strongly progressive relative to this filtration. Continuity of their paths, measurability of their initial values, and the coefficient integrability needed by the Itô formula are derived internally.

The fields are continuous in time and the complete paired configuration \((x,y)\in C\times C\). Compactness gives bounds on each finite horizon; no global bound or Lipschitz constant is assumed. Their signs are included in \(b_X,b_Y\); no separate tangency premise is imposed for this identity.

The temperature \(\lambda\) is one fixed nonnegative real number. The coordinate equations use the completed progressive \(L^2\) Itô integral with the same scalar coordinate of \(B_i\) in both equations, for every coordinate and every time on each horizon outside one null event for that horizon.

Process times are nonnegative. For the real-time Lean functions, negative time is clamped to zero. The interval integral is oriented, so the two-time identity uses arbitrary \(a,b\ge0\) without an ordering condition.

formulae.label: Shared Brownian SDEs and exact expected chord-energy balance
formulae.tex: \begin{gathered}P_x=I-xx^\top,\quad \delta_i=X_i-Y_i,\\ dX_i=[b_{X,i}(t,X,Y)-\lambda(d-1)X_i]dt+\sqrt{2\lambda}\,P_{X_i}\,dB_i,\\ dY_i=[b_{Y,i}(t,X,Y)-\lambda(d-1)Y_i]dt+\sqrt{2\lambda}\,P_{Y_i}\,dB_i,\\ D(t)=\frac1N\sum_i\mathbb E\|\delta_i(t)\|^2,\quad R_4(t)=\frac1N\sum_i\mathbb E\|\delta_i(t)\|^4,\\ L(t)=\frac2N\sum_i\mathbb E\langle\delta_i(t),b_{X,i}(t,X(t),Y(t))-b_{Y,i}(t,X(t),Y(t))\rangle,\\ G(t)=L(t)-2\lambda(d-3)D(t)-\lambda R_4(t),\\ D(b)-D(a)=\int_a^bG(s)\,ds\quad(a,b\ge0),\\ D\in AC([0,T]),\quad D^{\prime}(t)=G(t)\ (t>0),\quad D^{\prime}_+(0)=G(0).\end{gathered}

obligations.label: Actual supplied coordinate SDEs imply the exact expected energy balance and time regularity

bindings.boundary: Supplied solutions only: no process-existence, uniqueness, density, or pointwise PDE theorem is claimed. Temperature is one fixed nonnegative real number. Measurable time-varying temperature would need its own integral/AC-a.e. statement; it is not obtained by renaming this derivative theorem. The equality is dimension-general. A contraction sign requiring d>3, force estimates, or a closed coupling certificate requires additional downstream work. No independence of distinct particle drivers is used or derived. No two-sided derivative of the clamped real-time function is claimed at zero. No downstream actual-process adapter or removal of a downstream assumed Itô differential inequality has yet been completed. Joint measurability hX/hY remains explicitly present exactly as in the accepted source/signature. Its redundancy under strong progressivity is recorded for possible bounded purification; it was not silently removed.

assumption_deltas.source: Positive finite particle count; arbitrary ambient dimension, one probability space and usual filtration.
assumption_deltas.lean: N,d : Nat, hN : 0 < N, P : ProbabilityMeasure and SatisfiesUsualConditions.
assumption_deltas.reason: Dimension and normalization are literal; d=0 is vacuous for the supplied sphere-valued process. No d>=3 premise is added.

assumption_deltas.source: The two supplied sphere processes for each particle share the same standard vector Brownian driver.
assumption_deltas.lean: hB i gives the vector Brownian law relative to the common filtration; both equations use coordinateFamily (hB i).
assumption_deltas.reason: Compiler-derived bindings expose the same literal \(B_i\) coordinate and temperature in both stochastic integrals. No cross-particle independence is needed.

assumption_deltas.source: Jointly measurable, strongly progressive solutions with fixed nonnegative temperature and continuous full-configuration fields.
assumption_deltas.reason: Path continuity, finite-horizon coefficient bounds, noise L2 and drift integrability are derived internally, not added as inputs.

assumption_deltas.source: Original coordinate integral SDEs on every positive finite horizon, almost surely simultaneously at all its times.
assumption_deltas.lean: hEquation quantifies the positive horizon before one almost-everywhere event containing all times and finite coordinates.
assumption_deltas.reason: The nonlinear Ito identity, martingale centering and expectation balance are produced inside the proof.

assumption_deltas.source: Exact second- and fourth-moment observables and oriented balance on nonnegative times; derivative at positive times and right derivative at zero.
assumption_deltas.lean: Local literal definitions delta,D,R4,L,G use the original P; Real.toNNReal clamps negative times.
assumption_deltas.reason: No moment closure is used. The unordered interval identity is the oriented extension of the displayed ordered balance. The constant negative-time extension supplies no two-sided derivative claim at zero.
